title: Inheritance
points: Shared methods or state go in a parent class that children reuse.
Every child must be able to honour what it inherits. That is LSP.
trade: Tightest coupling in OOP: a parent change ripples into all children. Use it for true is-a; for has-a or code reuse prefer composition. Keep hierarchies shallow.
test: Why does Penguin extends Bird with a fly() in Bird break the inheritance rule, and what are two ways to fix it?
answer: Penguin inherits something it can't honour (LSP). Fix: move fly() into a FlyingBird subclass, or use composition (a Flyer capability or interface).
